thread:
Alex M: quick q about 429 semantics for per-route quotas — are we returning Retry-After in seconds or as an HTTP-date? our JS SDK currently expects seconds
Priya S: we landed on seconds in the spec draft (easier for SDKs) but double-checking if per-route headers follow the same shape as account/global headers
Jon K: implementation note: hosted currently emits seconds. example we return: 
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718235123
```
Marta L: X-RateLimit-Reset is epoch seconds UTC, right?
Jon K: yup epoch secs. SDKs should prefer X-RateLimit-Reset to compute backoff but fall back to Retry-After when Reset missing
Alex M: question about bursts — we use token-bucket. will X-RateLimit-Remaining ever be negative during a burst? some clients crash on negative ints
Priya S: we should not emit negatives. for bursts we cap Remaining at 0. we could add X-RateLimit-Burst but I'd rather avoid adding bespoke headers unless needed
Sam T: i'd prefer minimal surface area — Retry-After + Limit/Remaining/Reset is sufficient. clients can infer burst capacity from Limit + Reset cadence
Alex M: what about response body shape on 429? changing it will break older clients that parse error fields
Jon K: plan: keep body minimal and stable: {"error":"rate_limited","message":"please retry after X seconds"}. avoid adding nested objects.
Priya S: private/dedicated deployments should use the same header names to keep API contract uniform across hosted/dedicated/private
Marta L: if we ever rename a header, we should emit Deprecation and Sunset headers for one release cycle
Alex M: ok. SDK action items: Sam will make Retry-After parser accept both integer seconds and HTTP-date to be resilient
Sam T: yep will add that and fallback behavior. will also treat missing headers gracefully (use exponential backoff)
Jon K: i'll open a small PR to the API spec and add the header examples + a note about not returning negative Remaining.
Priya S: also FYI for routing: per-route quotas are enforced at the edge. fallback routing might return 429 from downstream variants — keep consistent 429 semantics there too
ratebot: applied config: default-tier per-route limit=600/min, burst_capacity=50 (logged)
Alex M: thanks everyone — i'll update product docs and the SDK checklist. :thumbsup:
Marta L: adding a quick test case to e2e: simulate burst and validate Remaining >= 0 and Retry-After present
Alex M: perfect, marking this resolved for now. If PR lands please ping in #eng-platform for review
